newsitem.title: UK: Smaller UK firms exports fall fastest in 6 yrs-CBI.
newsitem.headline: Smaller UK firms exports fall fastest in 6 yrs-CBI.

text.p: New export orders for Britain's small- and medium-sized firms fell at their fastest rate in six years over the last four months, the Confederation of British Industry said on Monday.
But because domestic demand continued to rise, both total new orders and output increased, albeit at the slowest rate for a year.

The CBI's survey, carried out in conjunction with accountants Pannell Kerr Forster, found a negative balance of 25 percent of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) reported an improvement in orders over the last four months.

In other words, 25 percent more of the 882 manufacturing companies surveyed reported a fall in export orders than reported an increase. In the four months to April, that balance was minus eight percent.

"Small and medium enterprises have been hit hard by the strength of sterling," said Tony Bonner, chairman of the CBI's SME council. "The seemingly inexorable rise in sterling is a disturbing development, placing a tight squeeze on exporters' margins."
The pound has rocketed more than 25 percent, on a trade-weighted basis, since last August, dragging exporters' prices higher.
Total new orders for SMEs rose at the slowest rate since July 1996. The current survey was conducted between June 20 and July 9.

The survey also found manufacturing output rose less than expected and its slowest rate for a year. Output is expected to pick up further over the next four months although expectations have not been fully met in more than two years.
"Despite a better domestic picture, total new orders and output are also suffering, increasing at their slowest rate for a year," Bonner said.

Britain's smaller enterprises also reported that domestic prices fell at their sharpest rate since October 1992. Over the next four months, prices are expected to slide more slowly than in the four months to July.

"Falling domestic prices and even more severely falling export prices present a challenge to gross margins and are clearly putting SMEs under pressure," said Raymond Blin, partner at Pannell Kerr Forster.
